hints: Notice the cylinder has the same cross-sectional area $A$ at the top surface with pressure $p_t$ and the bottom surface with pressure $p_b$.
Recall $p = F/A$, so each water pressure produces a force $F = pA$, with the top force acting down and the bottom force acting up.
Upthrust means only the net force from the water, so form $F_{up} - F_{down}$ and ask whether the block weight $W$ should appear in that water force.
walkthrough: Identify the water forces: top surface area $A$ at pressure $p_t$ experiences a downward force, bottom surface area $A$ at pressure $p_b$ experiences an upward force.
Use $p = F/A$ rearranged to $F = pA$ for a surface of area $A$ normal to the pressure.
Substitute: downward force on top is $F_t = p_t A$ and upward force on bottom is $F_b = p_b A$.
Upthrust is the resultant force from the fluid, so subtract: $U = F_b - F_t = p_b A - p_t A = (p_b - p_t)A$.
Do not include $W$: $W$ is the gravitational force on the wood, while upthrust is only the net pressure force from the water. This is option B.

options.A: Pressure has unit $\text{Pa}$ or $\text{N m}^{-2}$, so $(p_b - p_t)$ alone is not a force and cannot be the upthrust.
options.B: Net upward force from water is upward force $p_b A$ minus downward force $p_t A$, giving $(p_b - p_t)A$.
options.C: Weight $W$ acts downward due to gravity and is separate from upthrust, so it must not be subtracted from the water pressure force.
options.D: Weight $W$ is not part of the force exerted by the water, so it must not be added to the pressure-difference force.
